description: We are a multidisciplinary team of passionate about space, technology, and storytelling. For NASA Space Apps, we aim to build an engaging, scientifically grounded game for ages 7–18 that simulates establishing and managing a sustainable lunar outpost. We’re looking for members skilled in space science, 3D modeling, game design, animation, and STEM education.
summary: "MoonFall" is an interactive, browser-based pixel-art lunar mission simulator designed primarily for children aged 7-12 to bridge the gap between overly simplistic space content and complex technical material. It addresses the challenge of space education by using a two-phase learning approach, starting with "Cadet Training" across four core operational systems - power management, a hydroponics plant growth lab, ISRU water extraction, and radiation shielding - and advancing into "MoonFall Last Night", an emergency survival challenge where players navigate eight consecutive decisions to manage scarce resources like water, oxygen, and power during a simulated solar storm. Enhanced by a bilingual English and Bangla AI mission assistant named "AstroBee" that retrieves information from a verified database of NASA, NOAA, and peer-reviewed sources, MoonFall is important because it replaces abstract facts with hands-on gameplay, teaching young learners critical systems thinking, engineering trade-offs, and the real decision-making required to sustain human life beyond Earth.
details:
The Challenge We Address

Children are naturally curious about space, but educational resources about living and working on the Moon often fall into two extremes: overly simplified content with little scientific depth, or complex technical material that is difficult for young learners to engage with.

Understanding a lunar outpost requires more than knowing about rockets and astronauts. Future explorers must understand how interconnected systems sustain human life—and how to make difficult decisions when resources are limited.

MoonFall is an interactive, pixel-art lunar mission simulator that introduces children to the science and decision-making behind sustainable lunar exploration. Players manage real challenges such as keeping astronauts alive during power shortages, dividing limited water between drinking and oxygen production, and protecting the outpost during a solar storm.

Our Solution: Project MoonFall

MoonFall is a browser-based educational game designed primarily for children aged 7–12. Players take the role of a Junior Astronaut stationed at a lunar outpost, where they learn how its essential systems operate, conduct scientific experiments, and make decisions that affect the survival of the crew.

The game follows a two-phase learning approach, progressing from guided exploration to independent decision-making.

Phase 1: Cadet Training — Learn to Sustain a Lunar Outpost

Players complete four interactive training missions that introduce the essential systems of a lunar base.

1. Power Station — Understanding Energy Systems

Players learn how a lunar outpost generates, stores, and distributes power through interactive activities on solar panels, batteries, and energy management. They also troubleshoot simulated issues like lunar dust and prioritise essential electrical loads.

2. Plant Growth Lab — Food and Scientific Research

This mission introduces players to astronaut nutrition and food production beyond Earth.

  • Daily Meals: Players select packaged astronaut meals, learn about food preservation, rehydration, heating, nutrition, and waste management.
  • Hydroponics Experiment: Players establish a plant-growth experiment using a controlled growing system and treated lunar regolith. They monitor plant development, observe changes in colour, size, and condition, and compare their findings with results from an Earth-based lunar-regolith experiment.

This mission develops scientific observation and introduces the challenges of producing fresh food in a lunar environment.

3. ISRU Processing Facility — From Lunar Ice to Water and Oxygen

Players explore In-Situ Resource Utilisation (ISRU), learning how local lunar resources could support future exploration.

They operate a simulated extraction facility to locate ice-bearing regions, collect icy regolith, extract and purify water, and allocate recovered water between crew consumption, habitat requirements, and oxygen production.

Through electrolysis, players discover how water can be separated into oxygen and hydrogen. They must balance water availability, oxygen requirements, and energy consumption rather than simply maximising production.

4. Radiation Shielding — Protecting the Crew

Players learn about space radiation, solar particle events (SPEs), and galactic cosmic rays (GCRs).

During an interactive shelter-preparation activity, they position available materials such as water containers, food supplies, and other mission resources around the crew to improve simulated radiation shielding.

They also explore how lunar regolith could provide additional protection for permanent habitats and why astronauts must suspend surface activities during dangerous solar events.

Phase 2: MoonFall Last Night — The Ultimate Survival Challenge

After completing their training, players face a simulated solar storm emergency that puts their knowledge to the test.

During a routine mission outside the outpost, a space-weather warning signals an approaching solar particle event. The crew must return to safety and protect the lunar base.Players face eight consecutive decision-making challenges, with each decision influencing the conditions and available resources in subsequent stages.

A real-time telemetry sidebar displays important mission indicators, including oxygen, water, power, radiation conditions, and habitat status. Players must decide what to conserve, what to prioritize, and which systems can temporarily be shut down.

Other crew members provide advice and recommendations, but the final decisions belong to the player. Astrobee, the mission's AI assistant, provides contextual guidance throughout the experience.

Small interactive tasks between major decisions maintain engagement and reinforce the idea that every action has consequences.

The mission concludes with a performance assessment based on the player's decisions and the resulting condition of the outpost. Players can achieve different mission outcomes depending on how effectively they balance survival requirements.

Additional Features

Ask AstroBee — Bilingual AI Mission Assistant

AstroBee is MoonFall's English and Bangla AI-powered mission assistant. It helps players understand scientific concepts, explore mission procedures, receive contextual hints, and review their decisions without directly revealing quiz answers.

Built using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), AstroBee retrieves information exclusively from a verified scientific knowledge base containing:

  • 56 scientific fact cards.
  • 139 question-and-answer pairs.
  • 85 NASA, NOAA, ESA, and peer-reviewed references.

Its retrieval system uses BM25 search and a four-model fallback architecture comprising Qwen 3.8 27B, GPT-OSS 120B/20B, and Llama 3.1 8B. It also includes safety filters, code-based calculations, offline fallback responses, and live space-weather information from NASA and NOAA.

Development testing achieved 94% retrieval accuracy, 98% of development checks passed, zero quiz-answer leaks, and 38/38 automated backend tests passed.

Explore NASA Research

An integrated research section introduces players to ongoing NASA research related to lunar exploration, life-support systems, resource utilization, and future lunar habitats.

Base Upgrades

Players can explore emerging technologies being developed for future lunar settlements and understand how these technologies could improve outpost sustainability.

Research Hyperlinks

Scientific terms, technologies, and mission concepts link directly to relevant NASA research pages, allowing curious learners to explore beyond the game.

Meet the Crew

Here players meet four real-life space pioneers who guide them through the lunar missions: Chiaki Mukai, Sunita Williams, Rakesh Sharma, and Guion S. Bluford Jr.

The game honours their historic contributions to space exploration through short profiles to inspire the player.

An Important Note on Scientific Accuracy

Although MoonFall is designed for children, its scientific foundation is grounded in real research.

We do not use fantasy to misrepresent science. Instead, we use storytelling and gamification to make genuine scientific concepts easier to understand.

NASA research and scientific publications inform our mission scenarios, technologies, and learning materials. Where simplified numerical values or percentages are introduced for gameplay, they are treated as simulation parameters rather than actual NASA measurements.

The storytelling creates the experience; real science provides its foundation.

Target Audience

MoonFall is primarily designed for children aged 7–12, particularly students interested in astronomy, space exploration, science, and technology.

However, its interactive missions and accessible scientific explanations can also benefit educators, parents, and older learners looking for an introductory understanding of lunar outpost operations.

Benefits & Expected Impact

  1. Making Space Science Accessible
    MoonFall turns complex lunar science into interactive, story-driven gameplay that is engaging without losing scientific accuracy.
  2. Learning Through Decisions
    Players apply what they learn through resource management, energy conservation, oxygen production, and emergency response—understanding real trade-offs and constraints.
  3. Developing Scientific Thinking
    The hydroponics lab encourages observation and evidence-based conclusions, while other missions build systems thinking and problem-solving skills.
  4. Introducing Future Space Technologies
    Players explore real concepts such as ISRU, hydroponics, electrolysis, radiation shielding, lunar regolith use, and sustainable life-support systems.
  5. Breaking Language Barriers
    Bilingual AI assistance in English and Bangla makes scientific content more accessible to a wider range of learners.
  6. Accessible Across Devices
    As a browser-based game, MoonFall works on both desktop and mobile devices without requiring special hardware.

What We Hope to Achieve

  • Players meet real engineering: Fission grids, ISRU water extraction, and solar storm survival, taught through story without watering down the science
  • Decisions under pressure: As Commander, balance oxygen, power, and crew health to learn systems thinking
  • Inspire the Artemis Generation: Hands-on exposure to lunar engineering and NASA research for students who rarely get it
  • Scale into open science: More missions , harder trade-offs, classroom mode, and NASA-based data

Today’s player is tomorrow’s astronaut. 

Stack:

Frontend - HTML, CSS, JavaScript

Game Development - JavaScript (game logic, interactions, and mission systems)

UI/UX Design - Figma

Deployment - Vercel

AI Assistant Backend - Cloudflare Workers

AI Integration  - RAG, BM25 retrieval, LLM APIs

Video Production - Adobe Premiere Pro

AI Models and Services

AstroBee AI Assistant

  • Qwen 3.8 27B
  • GPT-OSS 120B
  • GPT-OSS 20B
  • Llama 3.1 8B

These models are integrated through a fallback architecture to support context-aware scientific assistance.

AI-Assisted Development and Content Creation

  • ChatGPT — Concept development, research assistance, writing, and visual asset generation.
  • Google Gemini Veo — Video generation.
  • Google Antigravity — Code development and programming assistance.

NASA and External Data Sources

NASA DONKI — Space Weather Database

The NASA Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI), accessed through the NASA API, provides space-weather information used to support MoonFall's solar-storm learning experience.

NASA Research and Educational Resources

NASA publications and research materials inform the scientific concepts and mission design, including:

  • NASA Human Health, Medical, and Performance Standards (NASA-STD-3001, Volumes 1 and 2).
  • NASA space-food systems and astronaut nutrition resources.
  • NASA lunar exploration and lunar habitat research.
  • NASA research on lunar resources and In-Situ Resource Utilization.
  • NASA research on space radiation and radiation shielding.
  • NASA Electrodynamic Dust Shield Demonstration.

NASA and NOAA Space-Weather Resources

Additional scientific information and space-weather references support AstroBee's verified knowledge base and its live information features.

NASA YouTube and Video Resources

Official NASA video content is integrated through the YouTube API to provide video previews and educational material in the Explore sidebar.

Scientific References used for game mechanism 

  1. Ewert, M. K., Chen, T. T., & Powell, C. D. — Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document.
  2. NASA — Human Health, Medical, and Performance Spaceflight Standards (NASA-STD-3001), Volumes 1 and 2.
  3. Colozza, A. J. — Small Lunar Base Camp and In Situ Resource Utilization Oxygen Production Facility Power System Comparison.
  4. Plants grown in lunar regolith present stress-associated responses — Communications Biology (2022). https://www.nature.com/articles/s42003-022-03334-8
  5. NASA — Space Food Systems and Food in Space. https://www.nasa.gov/ochmo/food-in-space/
  6. NASA — Space Food Systems. https://www.nasa.gov/directorates/esdmd/hhp/space-food-systems/
  7. NASA — Electrodynamic Dust Shield Demonstration.
  8. NASA — Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI). https://api.nasa.gov/
  9. NASA — Space Radiation Research and Human Exploration Resources.
  10. NASA and NOAA — Space-weather research and educational resources.

Besides these, many additional NASA resources were used as hyperlinks within the in-game dialogues. 

Project Platform

MoonFall is deployed as a browser-based application, with its game interface hosted on Vercel and the AstroBee AI backend deployed through Cloudflare Workers.

The architecture combines interactive game development, verified scientific information, and AI-assisted learning into a single educational experience.
